title: The Crooked Button
angle: Uncertainty about whether a small flaw matters can ease when attention shifts from its appearance to the job it needs to do.
paragraphs: On a coat with a newly replaced button, a few uneven stitches can take up the whole field of view. The thread crosses itself; the button sits a fraction off-center. Close up, the repair seems to be about those details.

Then the coat is worn. The button holds, the fabric gathers, and attention moves elsewhere. That shift doesn’t prove every flaw is harmless: a loose button matters if it falls off. A crooked one may not. Inspection and use are different scales of judgment, and the second can answer a question the first leaves hanging.

Uncertainty sometimes persists because a small detail is being asked to settle a larger question: Is this good enough? The answer depends on what the thing is for. A button needn’t become beautiful or symbolic. It only has to keep the coat closed—a modest test, and often a more useful one than staring at the stitches.
